title: "Software Engineering" Was Coined as a Deliberate Provocation (1968)
explainer: When NATO convened a conference in Garmisch, Germany in October 1968 to confront a perceived 'software crisis,' its organizers titled it a conference on 'Software Engineering' even though no such discipline really existed yet - the Study Group chose the phrase deliberately as provocative, to argue that building software should rest on the same theoretical foundations and practical disciplines as the established branches of engineering. That conference, and its 1969 Rome follow-up, played a major role in splitting what had been one undifferentiated field of 'computing' into the menu of named specializations - software engineering, systems work, applications development, and more - that a learner samples today. It's a useful check on assumptions: today's specialization boundaries are a fairly recent, somewhat deliberate historical invention, not a natural law of how software work has to be divided.
